title: 2 of the Best ETFs to Buy When Inflation Is Running Hot
author: Dave Kovaleski
description: With inflation rising to 3.4% in August and potentially climbing further, two actively managed ETFs are positioned to outperform during inflationary periods: the Avantis Inflation Focused ETF (AVIE), which invests in inflation-correlated sectors like energy and healthcare, and the VanEck Real Assets ETF (RAAX), which focuses on commodities and real assets. Both have demonstrated strong performance when inflation spikes, though they underperform during bull markets.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The ETF is specifically designed to outperform during inflationary periods and has demonstrated this with 19% year-to-date returns as inflation ticked back up in 2026. It holds quality stocks in inflation-correlated sectors with strong earnings characteristics.

The fund proved its value during the 2022 inflation spike, returning 1% while the S&P 500 fell 19%. It has also performed well year-to-date with 16% returns and maintains strong longer-term annualized returns of 19% over three years and 14% over five years.

title: Could This Mid-Cap GLP-1 Stock Be a Better Buy Than Eli Lilly?
author: David Jagielski, Cpa
description: Viking Therapeutics' GLP-1 drug VK2735 showed promising clinical trial results with 16-19% weight loss and strong maintenance rates, causing the stock to surge. While riskier than Eli Lilly due to its smaller $4.1B market cap and lack of approved drugs, Viking could offer significant upside potential through drug approval or acquisition by a larger healthcare company.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Positive clinical trial data for VK2735 showing strong efficacy (16-19% weight loss) and maintenance rates, recent stock surge, and potential for significant upside through approval or acquisition despite higher risk profile.

Acknowledged as a market leader in GLP-1 space with strong historical returns (400% in 5 years), but characterized as having limited future upside potential due to high valuation and large market cap, making it less attractive for growth investors.

title: Here's Where Wall Street Analysts See Eli Lilly's Share Price Going
author: Matthew Benjamin
description: Eli Lilly's stock has underperformed the broader market in 2026 despite a strong 5-year run, trading at 40x earnings. Wall Street analysts are modestly bullish with an average price target of $1,325 (11% upside), with 25 of 30 analysts recommending buy. The expanding GLP-1 market, projected to reach $190 billion by 2045, and Lilly's strong patent protection through the late 2030s support a positive outlook despite competitive threats from Novo Nordisk.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong market position with world's best-selling drug (tirzepatide), expanding GLP-1 market opportunity ($190B by 2045), robust patent protection through late 2030s, and 25 of 30 analysts recommending buy with average 11% upside target. Current valuation at 40x earnings is high but justified by growth prospects.

Identified as Lilly's main GLP-1 competitor with its own oral weight loss drug (Wegovy), representing competitive threat to Lilly's market dominance. However, no specific analyst sentiment or price targets provided for this company in the article.

title: Lilly Cut an Obesity Drug -- but the Move Shows How High Its Bar Has Become
author: Reuben Gregg Brewer
description: Eli Lilly discontinued development of a new GLP-1 weight-loss drug that failed to meet efficacy expectations. While GLP-1 drugs (Mounjaro, Zepbound, Foundayo) account for over 65% of the company's revenue, Eli Lilly is strategically preparing for future patent expirations by aggressively investing in its drug pipeline through acquisitions and in-house research, particularly in infectious diseases. The company's willingness to cut underperforming candidates and move quickly on acquisitions demonstrates strong long-term strategic positioning.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite cutting an underperforming drug candidate, the article frames this as a sign of strength and high standards. The company's dominant market position in GLP-1 drugs, aggressive acquisition strategy to diversify its pipeline, and proactive preparation for future patent expirations demonstrate strong strategic management and long-term shareholder value creation.

Mentioned as the first-mover in the GLP-1 space but lost market leadership to Eli Lilly due to supply chain issues and inferior patient outcomes. No new developments are discussed, warranting a neutral stance.

title: Viking Therapeutics Soared After Its Latest GLP-1 Data. Is It Too Late to Buy?
author: Adria Cimino
description: Viking Therapeutics released positive maintenance dosing data for its GLP-1 drug candidate VK2735, causing the stock to surge 35%. The company is positioning itself as a potential competitor in the $100 billion weight loss drug market dominated by Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk. Viking's dual GLP-1/GIP agonist could be the first oral formulation of its kind, with both injectable and oral versions available, offering advantages over current competitors.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company demonstrated strong clinical trial results with 97% weight loss maintenance at reduced dosing frequency. Stock surged 35% on the news. Positioned as potential market disruptor with unique dual agonist technology in both oral and injectable forms, offering competitive advantages in a high-demand market.

Currently dominates the GLP-1 weight loss market alongside Novo Nordisk with blockbuster products like Mounjaro and Zepbound. Mentioned as established market leader but no new developments or concerns highlighted in the article.

Co-dominates the GLP-1 weight loss market with products like Ozempic and Wegovy. Established as major player but no specific developments or concerns mentioned. Positioned as incumbent competitor to potential new entrant Viking.
